Prep plan for your Lincoln International final round, starting with the timeline:
- Three days before: confirm the format, who you'll meet, and the time zone. Pull up the Lincoln International job posting and list the skills it names. Each one needs a story from your own work.
- Two days before: write four stories with a number in each (situation, what you did, result). Practice them out loud, timed under two minutes each.
- The day before: review your resume line by line so you can explain every bullet. Prepare three questions for them about the team, the analyst's first-year work, and how success is measured.
- Day of: get there or log in early, have a pen and your questions ready, and keep water nearby.
Topics to cover for an analyst final round: why this firm and this role, a walkthrough of your most analytical project, how you handle ambiguous data, a time you disagreed and how it resolved, and a time you missed a deadline or made an error and fixed it.

What to practice out loud: the "tell me about yourself" pitch (60 seconds), each of your four stories, and one case or modeling question if the posting mentions one.

I don't have your resume, your confirmed facts, or the Lincoln International posting on file, so I can't tailor the stories to your experience yet. Paste your resume here and I'll read it, and I can pull the posting and interview questions for the role.
